change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: KeyError when the existing Integration has no metadata["sender"]
findings.body: `sender` is only written to metadata when the installation webhook supplied it (integration.py:376-377). `installation.py:44` already guards `"sender" not in integration.metadata`. Integrations created before this field existed, or without the webhook state, have no `sender`. For them `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises KeyError and the user gets a 500 instead of the error dialog. Use `.get("sender", {}).get("login")`. Also make sure a missing sender fails closed: `pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user")` could be None and must not be accepted against a missing value.

findings.title: Network errors in the OAuth exchange are not handled
findings.body: `safe_urlopen` (line 423) and `get_user_info` (line 434, which calls `raise_for_status` in sentry/identity/github/provider.py:16) are outside any try/except. A GitHub outage, a timeout or a revoked token gives a 500 rather than the `error()` dialog that the sibling failure paths return. Wrap both and return `error(...)`.

contracts.action: New OAuth login step before GitHubInstallation
contracts.before_after: The code mirrors the OAuth2 exchange but skips its error handling. It checks state against pipeline.signature, exchanges the code, then binds the GitHub login to the pipeline state.
contracts.visible_effect: The user is redirected to GitHub authorize, then continues to the app install, or sees the failed-dialog template.
contracts.failure_mode: Network or HTTP errors from safe_urlopen or get_user_info are unhandled and give a 500. A missing metadata sender also gives a 500 (reported).

summary: The user-verification flow works, but line 503 raises KeyError when an existing integration has no `sender` in its metadata, which gives a 500. The OAuth exchange also has no handling for network errors. The tests cover the new flow. The pipeline_advancer change is a harmless refactor.
